verdict.rationale: Mastra Knowledge stores pages in per-customer or per-team scopes. The scopes the server passes for each run decide what that run can read, and search only returns readable pages. Multiple agents can share one scope, and permissions can be set at the individual, team and org level, which gives shared group memory while keeping other scopes private. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of the isolation, detailed docs on individual-level private scopes beyond the announcement blog line, and clarity on how this interacts with per-agent conversational Memory privacy.

support.subject: As a developer, I can share selected memory across multiple agents or users (team or group memory) while keeping private memory private

citations.quote: Each customer's or team's pages live in their own scope, and the scopes your server passes for a run decide which ones it can read.
A research agent writes findings, a planning agent adds a plan under them, and a coding agent reads both from the same scope.
Search only returns pages the run can read, so a run that holds a different `org:` scope doesn't find Acme's page.
set permissions at the individual, team and org level.
a viewer reads, a contributor adds pages and notes, an editor changes pages, and an owner can also delete pages and move them between scopes.
